title: Willowshore Hinterland Feature (d10)
note: An unplaced hinterland place/feature for a wilderness scene (1 hex = 2 miles; mostly Specterwood forest, low Trimountains, rivers/lakes). Drawn from setting-canon hinterlands. The hinterlands feel wrong/haunted on the surface; their true (mindscape) nature is GM-ONLY — do not surface it. Reuse a named canon site when fitting, or generate a fresh feature of this type.

entries.value: Deep Specterwood forest hex (difficult terrain off-road) — dense, quiet, the canopy swallowing sound; the woods 'feel wrong' lately though no one says why.
River or creek course — the Ceiba's upper reach, Ceiba Creek, Dragonfly Creek, or the Duyue's headwaters; fords, log-jams, a half-rotted skiff.
Lake or pond — Gourd Lake (kappas dwell there; leave an offering), Mirror Lake near the monastery approach, or a still backwater fishers favor.
Trimountain slope or peak — the three peaks NW of town; the lowest holds the Great Willow, the highest is Green Silk Peak (~2,000 ft); thin air and old shrine-paths.
Old trail or road — the overgrown Pilgrim's Path NW toward Tan Sugi Monastery, the Apple Road south, or a rutted lumber track reclaimed by saplings.
Abandoned settlement site — the Old Village Expansion farmsteads (the stream there dries unpredictably), the reclaimed Lumber Camp by the Ceiba's source, or the burnt Canary Inn ruins.
Rocky / quarried ground — the Gorge of Fangs and Teeth (road and foundation stone), a scree field, or the difficult rough fields of the southern hinterland.
Ominous landmark — the Eyes of Fumeiyoshi (two barren sinkholes of gritty pooled water), a lone weathered shrine-stone, or a clearing where the birds have gone silent.
Ruin or sacred site — the shunned Tan Sugi Monastery up the Pilgrim's Path (reputed den of monsters and ghosts since the Night of Broken Blades), or a forgotten roadside shrine.
